title: The Most Colorful Mammal on Earth Wears Its Rank on Its Face

scenes.text: This animal's face tells you exactly who's in charge.
The mandrill. Blue ridges, a red stripe, and a rump to match. The most colorful mammal ever found in nature.
Testosterone drives the color. The males with the highest levels have the reddest faces, and they hold the top ranks.
The brightest, most aggressive males father most of the babies. Lower males stay duller, until the day they rise.
And they live in the biggest stable groups of any wild primate. One horde in Gabon was counted at 845, and once at 1,350.
Two-inch fangs, and nearly every wild male has broken his. The face says boss. The teeth say he earned it.

description:
Male mandrills carry blue and red faces that signal rank: the males with the most testosterone have the reddest faces, hold the top positions and father most of the offspring, while lower-ranking males stay duller until they rise.
In Gabon's Lopé National Park, hordes averaged about 620 animals and reached 845, probably the largest stable group of any wild primate; one temporary merger was counted at 1,350. Zoo males grow upper canines of about 2 inches, but of 12 wild males examined, only one had undamaged teeth.
Which animal would you say has the most striking face in nature?
subject: mandrill
first_comment: Females can escape a male by climbing trees too thin to hold him, so the top males also have to be the best at winning females over. Which animal has the most honest face?
